responsibilities: You know the dbt project, the new model structure and the most important source systems, and you work confidently with Claude Code and the skills in the repo.
Your first models are running in production, via branch, review and test, with documentation.
You can trace a core metric (for example revenue or active contracts) from the source all the way to the report.
You implement model tickets in dbt independently, from requirement to release, with tests and documentation as part of "done".
You build metrics in the semantic layer (MetricFlow) and move Metabase questions onto certified models.
You give and receive reviews, learning from the senior Analytics Engineer and your peers.
You own a business domain in the model (for example Product or Marketing) and are the point of contact for those teams.
The business teams answer recurring questions on these models themselves, without a ticket.
At mid level, you define metrics together with the business teams and contribute improvements to our standards.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: with tests and documentation as part of "done"
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Tests, reviews, documentation and certified models recur throughout; 'take on real responsibility fast' is the only speed phrase.
evidence.domain_risk: You can trace a core metric (for example revenue or active contracts) from the source all the way to the report.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: An energy retailer's internal analytics on revenue and contracts, with no regulatory, compliance or financial reporting language.
evidence.data_team_maturity: We are growing our Analytics Engineering team, and this is a great moment to join early.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing analytics engineering team with a dbt project, semantic layer and senior engineer is growing, which is a mid-stage function.
evidence.jd_authorship: You build metrics in the semantic layer (MetricFlow) and move Metabase questions onto certified models.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Outcomes name the tools (dbt, MetricFlow, Metabase, Claude Code), the workflow and the timeline, so the day-to-day work is clear.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: The business teams answer recurring questions on these models themselves, without a ticket.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The goal is a certified self-serve modelling layer that business teams query themselves.
evidence.autonomy_level: You start by shipping your first models and grow into owning a business domain over time.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role implements model tickets and learns from a senior engineer, with domain ownership as a 12-month growth goal.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Code is a core part of how you work, with skills and agents already set up in our repo.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is expected to use AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot in their daily modelling work.
evidence.testing_framing: You implement model tickets in dbt independently, from requirement to release, with tests and documentation as part of "done".
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Writing tests is part of the candidate's own definition of done.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The posting is framed around growth and delivery ('We celebrate mistakes as long as we learn from them'), with no risk or compliance register.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: move Metabase questions onto certified models
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role builds new models and metrics while migrating existing Metabase questions onto the new model structure.
evidence.language_gate: experience in a growing startup, and German.
